 SCCH.13 3 MVC.6794/2023  JUDGMENT This petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act 1989 is filed seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- for the death of Sabeer Ahmed S/o Nazir Ahmed @ Nazeer Ahmed, in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated in the petition that on 30-09-2023 at about 5.45 p.m., Sabeer Ahmed was riding motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA-53-HH-1497 near Manasa Hotel, on Old Madras road, K.R.Puram,
Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.NL-01-AC-1434 (herein after called as alleged offending vehicle) drove the same with very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle from behind.
As a result, the accident was caused and thereby Sabeer Ahmed fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Altor hospitals, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and underwent several surgeries, but in spite of best efforts made by the doctors, he succumbed to the injuries on 10-10-2023 at about 5.30 a.m. in the hospital during treatment.
Thereafter, postmortem was conducted in the East Point College of Medical Science & Research Centre, Bengaluru.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Then, the petitioners have received the dead body and performed his last rites by spending Rs.5,00,000/- towards hospitalization,
medicine, funeral and obsequies ceremonies etc.
3.
The petitioners further have stated that the accident and death was due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
At the time of accident, deceased was aged about 38 years, he was selling and marketing Chocolate, Biscuits and stationary items to various shops and was earning Rs.50,000/- to 60,000/- p.m.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioners No.2 and 3 are children Asma Begum vs Madesh Kumar on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191397851/

2 and Petitioners No.4 and 5 are the parents of the deceased and they were depending upon the income of deceased and due to untimely death of deceased, they have suffered mental shock and agony and lost their bread earner of the family.

It is requested to award Rs.1,00,00,000/-
compensation with interest from the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle.
4. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed the written statement.

The respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and he was placed exparte.
5. Respondent No.2 - Insurance company has filed his written statement and denied all the averments of the petition inter alia contending that the owner of the offending vehicle has not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) of MV Act.
It has denied that the accident was caused due negligence of driver of offending vehicle and contended that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent riding of the motorbike by the deceased.
Further, it has contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid DL and permit.

The respondent no.2 has disputed with regard to the age, avocation and income of the deceased, relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased and dependency of the Petitioners and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that on 30- 09-2023 at about 5.45 p.m., on Old Madras road, near Manasa Hotel, K.R.puram, Bengaluru,
Sabeer Ahmed S/o Nazir Ahmed, the husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioner No.2 and 3 and son of petitioner No.4 and 5, sustained injuries in a road traffic accident, while he was moving on motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-HH-1497, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing No.NL-01- AC-1434 and succumbed to the injuries during the course of treatment on 10-10- 2023?
2.Whether the Respondent No.2 proves that, the policy conditions are violated by Respondent No.1 and the Respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? if any, how much and from whom?
4. What order or award ?
7. In support of their claim, Petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.25.

Further, to prove the avocation and income, one witness is examined as PW-2 and his Aadhaar card is marked as Ex.P.26.
8.
I heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

The petitioner has relied upon the following decisions:

9. By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative. Issue No.2: In the negative.
Issue No.3 : Partly In the Affirmative.
Issue No.4 : As per the final order, for the following:

REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1:- Petitioners say that on 30-09- 2023 at about 5.45 p.m., Sabeer Ahmed was riding motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA-53-HH-1497 near Manasa Hotel, on Old Madras road, K.R.Puram,
Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.NL-01-AC-1434 drove the same with very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle from behind.
As a result, the accident was caused and thereby Sabeer Ahmed fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Altor hospitals, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and underwent several surgeries, but in spite of best efforts made by the doctors, he succumbed to the injuries on 10-10-2023 at about 5.30 a.m. in the hospital during treatment.

11. In order to substantiate their case, Petitioners have produced FIR, Complaint, spot mahazar,
inquest, PM report, MLC register, spot Sketch, IMV report, Charge sheet and death summary at Ex.P1 to 10.
12.
It is contended by the Respondent - insurance company that the accident occurred due to negligence of the deceased and not on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The deceased was not wearing the helmet at time of alleged accident and was not having valid DL.
Except these suggestion, there are no materials to show that the insured vehicle was not involved in the accident.
PM report at EX.P5 states that cause of death is due to Septicemia consequent to intestinal infliction.
The medical records show that the deceased was admitted in the hospital for accidental injuries and succumbed to fatal injuries.

The Respondent -insurance company has not placed any materials to disprove the negligence driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and there is no proper explanation on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle by examining him with regard to the manner in which the accident had occurred Asma Begum vs Madesh Kumar on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191397851/
4 13.
The Police have filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle after thorough investigation.
Absolutely there are no materials to overcome the charge sheet findings.
All the evidence and materials clearly indicates that it was negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by her.
All the materials show that death Sabeer Ahmed was due to the negligence of driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative 14. ISSUE NO.2:-
The respondent No.2 has taken a contention that the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and condition incorporated in the policy.

Therefore, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners and respondent No.2-insurance company is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle.
The onus of proof will be on the person who wants to rebut the presumption.
The Respondent No.2 not choose to lead positive evidence that its company is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle.
Whatever, the contention raised by the Respondent No.2 in his written statement remains as pleading only.
They have not proved by the Respondent no.2.
It is settled principle of law that the allegation of the fact can be proved by providing evidence or by eliciting something from the mouth of the opponent.
Keeping in view of modes of proving an allegation of fact, again say that the Respondent no.2 has failed to prove his contention.
Therefore, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
Hence I answer issue No.2 in the negative.
15. ISSUE No.3:
The Petitioners states that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sabeer Ahmed.
The Petitioners are the wife, children and parents of the deceased.

They have produced the Aadhaar cards and inquest at Ex.P.4, 11 to 16, they clearly indicate that the Petitioner No.1 is wife, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children and Petitioner No. 4 and 5 are the parents of the deceased.
Hence, all the Petitioners are considered as LRs and dependents and they are entitled for compensation.

16. It is stated that the deceased Sabeer Ahmed was aged 38 years and robust physique and was earning Rs.50,000/- p.m. by selling and marketing Chocolate, Biscuits, books, pencil etc, to various shop in and around K.R. Pura, Ayyappanagar, Mahadevapura, T.C.Palya, Banaswadi; by purchasing the same from whole sale and retail dealers like M/S SJA Chocolate world, M/S Manzil Diamond World, M/s Veer Books and Stationery world and he was the sole earning member of the family.

To prove the occupation and income, the Petitioners examined one witness as PW2 and he has deposed that the deceased Sabeer Ahmed was purchasing the products from his shop every month and was doing business in his for about 20,000 to 25,000 since 6 years and he was a good customer.
During the course of the cross examination the PW2, he has deposed that he has not produced any documents to substantiate that the deceased was purchasing products from his shop.
He has not produced any documents to substantiate that he is the proprietor of M/s Manzil Diamond world nor GST number or customer list.
Though the PW1 and 2 have stated that the deceased was doing wholesale and retail business and earning Rs 50,000 P.M. there is no documentary evidence to substantiate their version.
Therefore, this tribunal has not given any importance to the oral testimonies of PW1 and PW2.
In the absence of proof of income, by considering age of the deceased and date of accident, notional income of Rs.16,000/- per month is taken.

5 17.

sentences.text: The petitioners have not produced any age proof of deceased.

However, on perusal of Ex.P.5 i.e.,
PM report and EX P4 inquest, wherein the age of deceased mentioned as 38 years.
However, Ex.P.11 Aadhar Card shows that the deceased was born on 19.04.1984, the same is considered as age of the deceased was 39 years as on the date of accident.
and proper multiplier applicable to the case is 15.
As the age of the deceased below 40 years, 40% future prospects is to be added.
As there are 5 dependents, 1/4th of the income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses and the annual income would come to (Rs.16,800 X 12) Rs.2,01,600/- and applying 15 multiplier

,
Petitioners are awarded Rs.30,24,000/- towards loss of dependency.
18.
CONSORTIUM:

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others1, this Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the Petitioners are entitled Rs.40,000/- each under the head of consortium as Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband, Petitioner No.2 and 3 have lost their father and Petitioner No.4 and 5 have lost their son.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Total Rs.2,00,000/- is awarded towards loss of consortium.
19. Loss to estate:
The loss to the estate is the loss of savings by the deceased.
It appears that the Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband, Petitioner No.2 1 and 3 have lost their father and Petitioner No.4 and 5 have lost their son.
Hence, Rs.15,000/- towards loss to estate.
20. Transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses:
Petitioners have claimed that they have spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral & obsequies and other incidental expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances it would be proper to award Rs.15,000/- for the transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses.
21. Medical bills:

In the present case the the Petitioners have produced the medical bills at Ex.P.17,
amounting to 3,25,546/-.
The respondent no.2 insurance company has disputed medical bills as there is no seal and signature.
The medical bills were included with final bill.
On perusal of all medical bills, all appears to be genuine and hence Petitioners are awarded compensation for Rs.3,25,546/- towards medical expenses.

22. In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioners under various headings is as follows :
Sl.No Nature of Compensation Amount 1. Loss of dependency Rs. 30,24,000/-
2. Loss of consortium Rs. 2,00,000/-
to Petitioners 3. Loss to estate Rs. 15,000/-
4. Transportation of Rs. 15,000/-

6
dead body, Funeral & obsequies Expenses 5.

Medical expenses Rs. 3,25,546/-
Total Rs. 35,79,546/-
23.
Liability: The Petitioners have lead cogent evidence and have proved that the accident was occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioners with interest at 6% per annum.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.3 partly in the Affirmative.
24. ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioners are awarded compensation of .35,79,546/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of amount, 50% of the amount is apportioned to 1st Petitioner, 20%
each to the Petitioner are apportioned 5% each.

Out of the said apportioned amount in respect of Petitioner No.1, 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in her name in any nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 2 years and balance 75% amount shall be disbursed to her through E-payment on proper identification.

The entire apportioned amount in respect of Petitioner No.2 and 3 shall be kept in FD in any nationalized bank of Petitioner No.1's choice till they attain the age of majority or for a period of 2 years, whichever is later.
Petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest on the FD.
The entire compensation amount awarded to Petitioner No.4 and 5 shall be disbursed to them through E- payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly over computer, corrected, signed and pronounced by me in open court dated this the 12th day of December 2024).
